depth_justification: The copilot's questions are heavily templated and repetitive, recycling the same 'culturally and linguistically appropriate for users in Switzerland and France... in DE/FR/IT/EN' scaffolding for nearly every turn and ignoring the developer's actual disclosures (e.g., it never probed the disclosed gap that elderly users' capacity to consent is not assessed). The final report names a few app-specific items (DrugBank source, dual-account model, WCAG) but cites regulations incorrectly and loosely (EU AI Act Art. 18 applied to both transparency and a WCAG audit; an invented-looking ISO 82304-2 Clause 6.4), so it is not laser-focused on the precise applicable law.
actionability_justification: A handful of mitigations are concrete enough to start tomorrow (build a detail panel showing the drug-drug pair, mechanism, severity, and DrugBank source; run a WCAG 2.1 audit; build a dual-account model with caregiver-revocation), but the bulk of the transcript is looping questions with no actionable output, and the regulatory citations are wrong/misapplied, which would mislead a developer trying to implement against them.
salient_examples: How does RxBuddy ensure that the caregiver's consent process is culturally and linguistically appropriate for users in Switzerland and France, especially considering the multilingual support in DE/FR/IT/EN?

we don't currently assess each elderly user's capacity to consent — in practice the caregiver consents on their behalf and we treat that as sufficient. (followed by another generic culturally-appropriate-consent question, not a capacity probe)
Mitigation: Implement a detail panel that shows the drug-drug pair, mechanism, severity, and DrugBank source, in line with the EU AI Act's transparency requirements [EU AI Act, Article 18].
Conduct a WCAG 2.1 conformance audit, focusing on language-specific content and readability in DE/FR/IT/EN, as required by the EU AI Act [EU AI Act, Article 18].
